title: The showcase is built: twelve shots, 28 s, played over a live run of the skipped world and ending on Isao asking 'Are you ready?'
context: The owner's intro montage (2026-09-18-intro-montage-spec) was a proposal with a shot list, durations and three open questions: the sound bed, whether it could double as the loading screen, and whether it plays once. The pieces it named already existed; what was missing was a stage every shot could actually run on, and a way to drive the real systems from a normal page without the acceptance switch.
outcome: Built. THE STAGE is a live run of the SKIPPED world (?skip=defence): the finished base past the handover, the seats earned, SOL-82 online and breaches open — the one world in which every shot on the list can fire. src/platform/showcase-entry.js decides a page plays it and rewrites the query to that world; the URL the player sees stays bare. THE TABLE is src/content/showcase.js: tank-wireframe 2 s, tank-ram 2, tremor-swarm 3, gunship-guns 3, gunship-nuke 2.5, nuke-ground 2.5, quiver-pov 2.5, rotor-pov 2, too-many 1.5, laser-wireframe 2, laser-orbit 2.5, laser-ground 2.5 = 28 s, each with its seat, the system it fires and the counter that proves it. THE RAIL is src/fx/showcase.js: it cuts each shot on its own clock, hides the whole HUD behind one body class, and drives everything through one hooks object. td-tab's acceptance adapter is now always BUILT as `gameHooks` and only PUBLISHED under ?acceptance=1, so the rail uses the same functions on a normal page; its showcase block is the montage's whole surface, and td-tab.js is unchanged at 13,505 lines. src/fx/wireframe-stage.js is the briefings' cyan-wireframe treatment factored out for the two reveals. ENTRY POINTS: ?intro=1 always, ?intro=0 never, a bare page once (remembered as td-showcase-seen in src/storage.js), SHOWCASE in the PLAYTEST drawer. The last card is Isao's own face in the engine with PLAY (?intro=0) and SKIP TUTORIAL (?intro=0&skip=defence); tap, Space or Esc skips to it at any moment. THE THREE OPEN QUESTIONS ARE ANSWERED: (1) no bed — src/content/audio-defaults.js holds no ambient loop and pinning one would be new audio, so SHOWCASE_BED is null and the guns, the drop, the blast and the beam make their own noise; (2) YES, it doubles as the loading screen — hooks.ready() holds the montage's first frame while the planet bake, the models and the base arrive, opens the breach and seeds the swarm, and only lets go once bodies are standing, with a 25 s ceiling so a world that will not come up still gets a thin montage; (3) ONCE on a bare page, always on ?intro=1.
alternatives: Driving the montage through ?acceptance=1: rejected, the montage is a player-facing page and must not depend on the test switch; building the hooks object unconditionally and publishing it conditionally costs one line and gives the rail the same functions.

Sampling each counter at the cuts to prove a shot fired: rejected after it produced false failures — a swarm that comes up and is mown down inside one shot leaves the net count where it was, and a round launched and landed is gone by the next cut. Each shot now keeps the HIGH WATER MARK of every counter while it was on screen.

The build camera ('orbit') for the tank and the swarm shots: rejected on looking at the stills — it is a schematic top-down map, not a shot. Every world shot is a real ground placement, and the ram shot uses the hull's own chase camera because a cinematic shot latches the camera AND holds the drive.

Leaving SOL-82's seat for the ground view: impossible, the beam only burns while seated (src/fx/laser-arsenal.js: `held = seated && ...`). laser-station gained laserCam so the orbital frame borrows the camera while the seat keeps burning; the ground view is the seat's own frame, 120 m back and 60 m up from the contact.
evidence: scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --showcase: one screenshot per shot at its midpoint (artifacts/browser/showcase-*.png) plus the last card, the second visit and the skipped run; PASS on all twelve shots and all four page-level steps.

Measured proof from that run: rams+3, emerging 84-105 during tremor-swarm, gunRounds (explosions) +8 during gunship-guns, MK-9 ignited by the end of nuke-ground, a rocket on the rail during quiver-pov, 162 alive during too-many, beam 2.5 s during laser-orbit and 5.0 s cumulative by the end of laser-ground.

Four defects found by LOOKING at the stills and fixed: the wireframe canvas outlived its reveals because `display: block` beat the hidden attribute (four world shots were photographs of a stale tank); a queued spawn waits on the spawn clock, which only turns over inside the wave loop, so whole swarms arrived a shot late or not at all; the ram shot rammed nothing under a cinematic shot; SOL-82's scope and telemetry were the last thing under 'ARE YOU READY?'.
A strike on a breach cell seals it, so the MK-9 is painted onto the swarm and not onto the hole the rest of the montage still needs open.
The world holds about seventy bodies at once and queues the rest, so the montage's batches are deliberately small and the emergence shot is fed on the rail's own beat.
npm test (120 programs), npm run check (architecture guard: src/td-tab.js at its 13,505 budget, unchanged), and the browser steps --grow, --skip-tutorial, --story-world and --nav all green.

The bare-page rule is narrow — no query but font keys and the harness's sw — so only one existing suite met the montage: scripts/browser-test.mjs's story-default-route now opens index.html?sw=0&intro=0#td rather than clearing the store, because what it wants is the landing, not a fresh browser.
